packet.claim: The recovery kernel's cell grammar and rewrite execution are inconsistent for inputs containing a fenced object followed by prose or another object.
packet.execution_evidence: The provided test campaign results show INVALID_INSTANTIATION for proposals 3a3ffd2295cea743, ba1632743be8e4d5, d2b9bbc3bb6439e5, c883056725f16492, de585053b0a58e84, 9919b2230d4cbfc6, 604b932e83eff54f, and a moved result for 9237691326ad9586.
packet.expected: Rewrites that add or remove a trailing part should be valid when the resulting text is still a cell of the grammar, and the recovered object should remain unchanged for additions after a complete fenced object.
packet.observed: Several rewrites are marked INVALID_INSTANTIATION with details like 'the rewritten text is no cell of the grammar' or 'the input is not the cell it names', even when the rewritten text appears to be a valid cell; one case (fence[ A B ] with added C) unexpectedly changes the recovered object from {"b":2} to {"c":3}.
packet.scope: Recovery kernel inputs where a fenced JSON object is followed by prose or another object, and a rewrite adds or removes a trailing part.
packet.source_basis: recover_json_object: 'Every top-level balanced object in the text is a candidate... The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one, else the last top-level object in the text.'
packet.uncertainty: The exact grammar definition for 'cell' is not provided, so some INVALID_INSTANTIATION results may be correct if the grammar intentionally disallows certain sequences; the moved result for fence[ A B ] with added C may be intended if the last object wins, but it conflicts with the 'unchanged' expectation.
